title: Working at Redwood — hiring, onboarding, roles, career ladders, benefits & internal tools (People Ops guide)
author: Sophie Martinez
body:
Purpose:

This People Ops guide consolidates the core Company Handbook sections teams reference when hiring, onboarding, and growing people at Redwood. It is intended as the canonical, evergreen page for role frameworks, benefit summaries, hiring process norms, the standard new-hire 30/60/90 plan, and internal tools/access patterns. Team-specific addenda should link back to this page.

Audience:

- People managers and individual contributors across Engineering, Product, Design, Sales, Customer Success, and People Ops.
- Recruiters, hiring committee members, and People Ops partners.
- New hires and people who support onboarding.

Quick links (sections):

1) Roles & career ladders
2) Benefits & perks summary
3) Hiring process & interview guide
4) New hire onboarding and 30/60/90 plan
5) Internal tools, access & troubleshooting
6) Policies, escalation, and contacts

1) Roles & career ladders

Overview:
Redwood uses a level-based career framework across functions that describes scope, expected outcomes, competencies, and promotion signals. Managers must maintain team-level expectation docs and attach role templates to job requisitions.

Core ladders (high level):
- Engineering IC: IC1 (Associate) → IC2 → IC3 (Senior) → IC4 (Staff) → IC5 (Principal) → Distinguished Engineer.
- Engineering management: EM1 (Eng Manager) → EM2 (Senior Eng Manager) → EM3 (Director) → EM4 (VP).
- Product & Design: PM1 → PM2 → PM3 (Senior PM) → Principal PM; Designer I → Designer II → Senior Designer → Staff Designer.
- Cross-functional functions (Sales, CS, Solutions, People Ops, Finance): entry → mid → senior → lead / manager, with role-specific competency maps.

Promotion signals and evidence (standard):
- Clear increase in scope or complexity of problems owned.
- Consistent delivery against competencies for the target level (execution, ownership, influence, mentorship).
- Artifacts that demonstrate impact: PRs, architecture/design docs, metrics dashboards, customer feedback, and peer/manager feedback.

Promotion process (summary):
1. Manager prepares a Promotion Packet (role profile, 2–4 artifacts, manager write-up, peer feedback).
2. Packet submitted to Promotions workspace; People Ops schedules a calibration panel (quarterly).
3. Panel outcome recorded and communicated with next steps or development plan.

2) Benefits & perks (summary)

Philosophy: Competitive compensation, market-aligned benefits, and programs to support wellbeing, family leave, and continuous learning. Benefits are reviewed annually.

Highlights:
- Health: Medical, dental, vision (US plans) and country-equivalent options globally; HSA/FSA where available.
- Time off: 20 days PTO baseline (pro-rated first year), 12 company holidays, 5 discretionary mental health/volunteer days.
- Parental leave: Primary caregiver up to 16 weeks paid; secondary caregiver 6 weeks paid; phased return and transition stipend.
- Financial: 401(k) matching (US), equity grants at hire and periodic refreshes tied to role and performance.
- Learning: $2,000 annual L&D stipend per employee, internal learning weeks, paid conference budget for managers.
- Remote & wellbeing: Monthly home office stipend, wellness allowance, Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

Enrollment and help:
- Enroll via the Benefits portal within 30 days of start. For exceptions and clarifications, contact benefits@redwood.com.

3) Hiring process & interview guide

Goal: Fast, fair, and evidence-based hiring. Hiring is owned by the hiring manager, recruiter, and People Ops partner. All candidate data is handled in compliance with privacy and EEO rules.

Stages and owner responsibilities:
1. Requisition creation: Hiring manager creates requisition in Workday with job profile and salary band; People Ops approves headcount.
2. Sourcing & initial screen: Recruiter sources and runs a 30-min screen, populates the candidate tracker and scorecard.
3. Interview loop: Typical loop is 3–4 interviews (technical / role exercise, system design, behavioral). Use standardized rubrics and scorecards.
4. Hiring committee & calibration: Committee (including at least one calibrated interviewer from another team) reviews scores and recommends decision.
5. Offer and background checks: People Ops prepares offer within band and initiates background checks and eligibility verification.

Fairness and quality rules:
- Interviewers complete Unconscious Bias training annually.
- Avoid illegal/disallowed interview topics.
- Share role rubrics with candidates on request.

Recommended SLAs:
- Requisition approval: 2–5 business days.
- Move from first screen to technical loop: within 10 business days.
- Offer issuance to acceptance: target within 7 business days.

4) New hire onboarding & 30/60/90 day plan

Before day 1 checklist:
- Complete HR paperwork (tax forms, direct deposit) in People Ops portal.
- Enroll in benefits within 30 days.
- Confirm equipment shipment; verify Slack and Okta SSO connectivity.

Week 1 (Day 1–7): Orientation and foundations
- Day 1: People Ops welcome, executive welcome, team introduction, workstation setup.
- Week 1: Security training, code of conduct, product orientation, and team-specific onboarding activities. Manager assigns a buddy.

30/60/90 plan — manager and new hire responsibilities:
- 0–30 days: Setup and learn core systems, review product/architecture, ship a small scoped contribution. Success = environment ready and first PR merged.
- 30–60 days: Take ownership of a small feature or customer issue and present a plan. Success = feature delivered or customer outcome improved.
- 60–90 days: Drive impact on a cross-team metric and begin mentoring others. Success = measurable metric improvement and clear ownership.

New hire checklist (key systems):
- Identity: Okta SSO, MFA set up.
- Communication: Slack join and channel introductions.
- Code and infra: GitHub org membership, CI runner access, repo permissions.
- Tracking & docs: Linear/JIRA, Confluence access.

5) Internal tools, access, and troubleshooting

Identity and access management:
- Okta is the central identity provider. Group memberships and app assignments via People Ops Access Portal.
- MFA required for all employees; hardware keys recommended for high-scope roles.

Core tools and onboarding pointers:
- Slack: Channel naming conventions (ops-*, eng-*, product-*, cs-*). #announcements is company-wide.
- GitHub: Product and infra repos live in the Redwood org. Request access through the Developer Access form; follow branch/PR conventions in Engineering Standards.
- CI/CD: Pipelines run on GitHub Actions and use self-hosted runners for heavy workloads. See eng-infra CI runbook for troubleshooting and reruns.
- Issue tracker: Linear for engineering/product teams; use consistent labels for priority/area/sprint.
- Observability: Datadog for infra and dashboards, Sentry for app errors; access granted by on-call leads or service owners.
- Confluence: Canonical documentation store. Follow Page Ownership guidance for edits.

Access request flow (summary):
1. Identify needed access and owning team.
2. File a request in the Access Portal with business justification and duration.
3. Owning team approves or asks for clarification within 3 business days.
4. People Ops escalates overdue requests.

Common troubleshooting steps:
- SSO issues: Clear cache, try incognito, collect Okta logs and email idp-support@redwood.com.
- GitHub access problems: Verify org membership and 2FA; request dev-access if missing.
- CI failures: Check runner health dashboard and logs before filing infra tickets.

6) Policies, escalation, and contacts

Required reading and policy links:
- Code of Conduct (mandatory at hire).
- Security & Acceptable Use (required for any infra access).
- Time off and parental leave policy.
- Performance management and PIP guidelines.

Key contacts and escalation matrix:
- People Ops general: people-ops@redwood.com
- Benefits & payroll: benefits@redwood.com
- IT & device support: it-support@redwood.com
- Identity & SSO: idp-support@redwood.com
- For unresolved manager escalations: Director of People Ops (cc HR Business Partner).

Appendix: templates and examples (where to find)
- Promotion packet checklist: role profile, 2–4 supporting artifacts, manager write-up, peer feedback, proposed outcomes.
- Hiring templates & scorecards: People Ops > Hiring workspace.
- Team-specific ladders: team wikis under /confluence/company-handbook/[team-name]-ladders.

Revision history:
- 2024-08-12: Guide created by People Ops.
- 2025-05-02: Parental leave and equity refresh guidance added.
- 2026-02-10: Updated CI/CD runner guidance and access flows.

Questions or suggestions: open an edit request on this page or email people-ops@redwood.com.
